question: Breach of EU environmental law due to mining waste being discharged into the Guadalquivir and the serious risk this poses to Natura 2000 protected areas

The Sanlúcar de Barrameda City Council, other riverside municipalities and collectives such as Salvemos el Guadalquivir (Protect the Guadalquivir) and Salvemos Doñana (Protect Doñana) have long been warning that mining waste discharged into the Guadalquivir is severely polluting the riverbed and estuary, threatening biodiversity and traditional economic activity such as fishing, shellfish harvesting and agriculture.
The environmental deterioration of the Guadalquivir and the Doñana reserve is persistent, highlighting a structural problem of a lack of effective protection12.

Mining waste discharges – the cumulative effects of which are simply being ignored by the Andalusian regional government – are in breach of the Water Framework Directive, affect the Natura 2000 network (including Doñana (ES6150009), sites of Community importance, special areas of conservation and biosphere reserves) and fail to comply with Directive 2006/21/EC and the objectives of the Nature Restoration Regulation.

Given that various scientific reports warn that the volume of discharged waste could increase tenfold in the coming years – with several mining sites in operation simultaneously – and in view of the guiding principles of precaution and prevention: 1.
Is the Commission aware of mining waste currently being discharged, the effects of this and the potential for the situation to worsen due to planned projects?

Will the Commission formally request information from the Spanish authorities and demand an independent scientific investigation, as requested by platforms such as Salvemos el Guadalquivir and Salvemos Doñana?

Written question E-3692/2008 to the Commission, ‘Pollution in the river Guadalquivir’ (https://www.europarl.europa.eu/doceo/document/E-6-2008-3692_EN.html). Written question E-001259/2024 to the Commission, ‘Attack on the environment in Andalusia: plan to discharge 80 billion litres of highly polluting waters into the River Guadalquivir’ (https://www.europarl.europa.eu/doceo/document/E-9-2024-001259_EN.html).
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (10.7.2026) The Water Framework Directive (WFD)1 requires Member States to ensure that mining discharges do not cause deterioration of surface water status or prevent the achievement of good status.

All point source discharges, such as mining waste, must receive prior authorisation with sufficiently stringent emission controls to prevent pollution and protect water-dependent Natura 2000 sites. The Extractive Waste Directive2 sets a high level of protection for the environment and human health.

It includes specific provisions aimed at preventing the deterioration of water status in accordance with the WFD, while leaving competent authorities a margin of discretion when applying those rules. Under the Habitats Directive3 Member States must avoid deterioration of natural habitats and species habitats, and significant disturbance of species for which Natura 2000 sites have been designated.

Any project, including mining waste discharges into rivers, likely to have a significant effect on Natura 2000 must undergo an appropriate assessment of its implications for the site. The competent authority may only approve the project after ascertaining that it will not adversely affect its integrity.

In line with its enforcement strategy focusing on systemic non-compliance4, the Commission considers it is the primary responsibility of the Spanish authorities to adequately enforce the above provisions of EU law. The Commission is aware of the concerns raised by the Honourable Member and notes that, according to available information, the Spanish Environmental Prosecutor has opened an investigation5.
In any event, the Commission intends to discuss bilaterally with Spain the implementation of the WFD during an upcoming structured dialogue.
1 Directive 2000/60/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council of 23 October 2000 establishing a

framework for Community action in the field of water policy, OJ L 327, 22.12.2000, pp. 1–73. 2 Directive 2006/21/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council of 15 March 2006 on the management of waste from extractive industries and amending Directive 2004/35/EC - Statement by the European Parliament, the Council and the Commission, OJ L 102, 11.4.2006, p. 15–34.

3 Council Directive 92/43/EEC of 21 May 1992 on the conservation of natural habitats and of wild fauna and flora, OJ L 206, 22.7.1992, pp. 7–50. 4 As set out in the Communication of 19 January 2017: EU law: Better results through better application C/2016/8600, OJ C 18, 19.1.2017, p. 10–20 and in the Communication of 13 October 2022: COM(2022) 518 final - Enforcing EU law for a Europe that delivers. 5 E.g.
